name: Grand-Place
description: Guildhall façades surround Brussels’ central square, a UNESCO site of ornate gables.

name: Atomium
description: A 1958 World’s Fair pavilion shaped as an iron crystal still opens viewing spheres and exhibitions.

name: Belfry of Bruges
description: A medieval bell tower rises over Bruges’ Markt. Climbers pass the carillon on the way up.

name: Cathedral of Our Lady
description: A Gothic cathedral with a soaring spire holds works by Rubens in Antwerp’s centre.

name: Citadel of Namur
description: Fortifications overlook the Meuse–Sambre confluence with tunnels and panoramic walks.

name: Bruges canals
description: Boat tours and footbridges weave through Bruges’ medieval waterways.

name: Graslei and Korenlei
description: Historic guildhouses line the river Leie in Ghent’s postcard harbour stretch.

name: Ardennes forests
description: Wooded hills, rivers and castles fill southern Belgium’s outdoor region.

name: Antwerp Zoo
description: One of the world’s older zoos sits beside Antwerp Central Station.

name: High Fens
description: Boardwalks cross peat bog plateaus in eastern Belgium’s nature park.

name: Sablon chocolate shops
description: Praline boutiques cluster around Place du Grand Sablon.

name: Brussels waffle stands
description: Street stands serve Brussels-style waffles with toppings near the Grand-Place.

name: Vlaeykensgang & nearby cafés
description: Alleys and squares near the cathedral hold cafés and Belgian fries stands.

name: Ghent Vrijdagmarkt eateries
description: Squares around Vrijdagmarkt fill with terraces serving Flemish classics.

name: Liège market snacks
description: Liège-style waffles and market stalls cluster around the historic centre.

name: Tomorrowland
description: A large electronic-music festival held at De Schorre park, usually across July weekends.
